summary:
Observed 2026-10-23 on the Home host (util-linux/libmount 2.42.4, `mount --version` lists `fd-based-mount`) during SC2 reserved-storage rehearsal (#4746; #4516 comments 6363317030 and 6363451287). A helper that ran `mount --internal-only --no-canonicalize --types ext4 --options nodev,nosuid,nodiscard -- /dev/loopN /proc/self/fd/<target_fd>` (to pin the target by a held fd) failed with the generic rc 32 `wrong fs type, bad option, bad superblock ... missing codepage or helper program`, although the kernel log showed `EXT4-fs: mounted filesystem` immediately followed by `unmounting filesystem`.

Cause (from `LIBMOUNT_DEBUG=all`): libmount 2.42 mounts through the new API; `fsmount` succeeds and creates a detached mount, then `move_mount(to=/proc/self/fd/9)` fails with EINVAL (the `/proc/self/fd/N` magic link is not followed, so the target is the link itself). The detached mount is released on close, which is the kernel's immediate `unmounting`, and libmount reports rc 32. The earlier hypothesis that libmount re-checks the target by path was wrong and was corrected by the debug output. Diagnosis was a scratch-only run (64 MiB image) with four cases: the helper's exact call (rc 32), the same with debug (32), `LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2=always` (classic mount(2), rc 0) and a plain path target (rc 0).

Rule: do not pass a `/proc/self/fd/N` magic link as the mount target to libmount with fd-based mounts. Mount on the path of a fixed, root-controlled target directory and compensate with identity checks. Before the mount: hold an `O_PATH` fd on the directory and `lstat` each path component (no symlinks, root-owned). After the mount: re-open the path, require the mounted root's `st_dev` to equal the loop filesystem, require the held fd's identity to be unchanged and still the covered directory, and require `findmnt` to show exactly one mount on that target from the expected source; anything else unmounts and fails closed. This was delivered as SC2 helper r3. `LIBMOUNT_FORCE_MOUNT2=always` also worked but was not chosen, because it leaves the fd target dependent on the legacy path.

Diagnostic tip: a generic mount rc 32 with a kernel log showing a successful mount followed at once by an unmount means the failure is after the mount syscall; read `LIBMOUNT_DEBUG=all` before changing the filesystem or device options.

Limits: only 2.42.4 was observed; the version where this began and whether later releases change it are not established. Other callers of `move_mount` with magic-link targets were not tested. The cited document only supplies the repository's generic failure-custody expectation for diagnostic execution; the findings rest on the cited issue comments, whose scratch log and scripts stay in Home custody. This is not authority for any mount.
title: libmount >= 2.42 fd-based mounts cannot target /proc/self/fd magic links; use a path target with held-fd identity checks before and after
